newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends higher on heavy short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends higher on heavy short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude snapped a two-session losing streak Wednesday on a feverish bout of short covering as bullish weather forecasts overshadowed bearish oil inventory data which for the most part had already been factored into prices.
"It was mainly a lot of short covering. People had already been expecting a build in crude," said Al Lindseth, trader with GSC Energy in Atlanta. Crude's volume was an active 146,845 lots.
April crude settled up 51 cents a barrel at $20.62.
April heating oil ended 1.25 cents a gallon higher at 54.08 cents while April gasoline settled 0.77 cent a gallon up at 64.63 cents.

"The weather forecast came in and that really turned things around. The market is getting long products," said a New York dealer, noting traders were setting long term positions in heating oil and gasoline.
The National Weather Services six to 10 day forecast starting March 18 called for below to much below normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the largest heating oil market in the world.

"I think there were some early hedgers who got in the market in heating oil because they did not want to miss the buying opoortunuty," said Lindseth, explaining some felt compelled to take advantage of the sharp decline in heating oil prices to build stocks for next winter season.

Meanwhile, the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Energy Information Administration (EIA) said Wednesday that crude stocks grew 5.2 million barrels. The American Petroleum Institute (API), the oil industry's trade group, also said Wednesday that crude stocks grew 6.84 million barrels.
Trader expectations were for a build of between two million and six million barrels, although the consensus was for a build of 3.5 million barrels. The data reflects the week ended March 7.

But, increased supply was already factored into the market. Crude prices have been under sharp pressure this week due to talk of a bevy of imports heading into the U.S. Gulf amid a weak crude market in Europe.
While the U.S. market is relatively firmer, crude demand is still tepid due to U.S. refinery maintenance.
"This market is trying to find a bottom," said one dealer of oil prices near term. The oil complex may still have to weather the effects of increased crude supply, analysts said.
Crude stocks were 168,000 barrels above year ago levels in the latest API report.
Salomon Brothers oil analyst Paul Ting noted in a March 10 report that crude inventories should continue to grow compared to year ago levels in March.
"We believe that the crude oil inventory pattern likely will send continuous bearish signals to the oil market," Ting said in the report.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
